This document describes the design of the functions forming the Rust library and
tracks the implementation status.

{{< include /docs/includes/_design-status.qmd >}}

## {{< var planned >}} `check()`

The `check()` function first reads and parses a `request.yaml` and a source
metadata file, checking that they contain the required keys. It then runs the
checks described below in order, returning a `CheckError` if any check fails.

```rs
/// Checks a request yaml against the source metadata file.
/// 
/// The checks include: 
///   - Required sections and keys are present in the request and source.
///   - Data package name and version in the request matches the source.
///   - The resources and columns in the request exist in the source.
///   - The row filters reference columns in the source and only uses 
///     allowed SQL operators.
/// 
/// Errors if the request and source file can't be read, or if any
/// check fails.
pub fn check(request: Path, source: Path) -> Result<(), CheckError> {
  let request = read_request(request)
  let source = read_source(source)
  // Required sections and keys are present.
  check_request_keys(&request)
  check_source_keys(&source)
  // Referenced data package has the same version and name as the source.
  check_package_name(&request, &source)
  check_package_version(&request, &source)
  // Referenced resources exist in the data package.
  check_resource_names(&request, &source)
  // The requested columns exist in the selected resources.
  check_column_names(&request, &source)
  // Row filters reference existing columns.
  check_row_filters(&request, &source)
  // Only allowed SQL operators.
  check_sql_operators(&request)

  Ok(())
}
```
